response.sql: SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) as record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM advancedbehavior ab2 JOIN transactionrecord tr2 ON ab2.translink = tr2.transreg JOIN trader t2 ON tr2.trdref = t2.tradereg) as share FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind;

assumptions.assumption: "Analysed trade records in the advanced behaviour data" counts individual records in the advancedbehavior table. Since advancedbehavior.translink is not declared unique, multiple analysis records may reference the same transaction; this count reflects analysis records, not unique analysed transactions.

alternatives.interpretation: Count the number of distinct transactionrecords that have been analysed (have at least one advancedbehavior entry), rather than the total count of analysis records in the advancedbehavior table.
alternatives.sql: SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) as record_count, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT tr2.transreg) FROM advancedbehavior ab2 JOIN transactionrecord tr2 ON ab2.translink = tr2.transreg JOIN trader t2 ON tr2.trdref = t2.tradereg) as share FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind;
